flags: PHONE MISSING: Franklin County Conservation 641-456-4375 (franklincountyia.gov Conservation & Parks page). The board's own old site franklincountyconservation.org (linked from mycountyparks) returns Cloudflare error 523.

WATERFRONT LEAD (up, stored not waterfront): Maynes Creek (~7 m wide on imagery, so creekside class) wraps the campground on the north and south. On the 2022 aerial map and Esri imagery the rear ends of the south-row pads (#6-#12) and the north pads (#14-#18) sit ~15-35 m from the creek across mowed lawn, with a fringe of bank trees (leafless in the frame) rather than a solid treeline; no road or day use between those pads and the creek. Pads point back toward the creek, so creekside is plausible for those rows; the bank trees and steep cut banks are the uncertainty. Leaving the value to the waterfront pass.

PULL-THROUGH: stored sites.pull_through=true (from note prose) is contradicted by the 2022 map and imagery, which show dead-end gravel spurs angled off the loop (back-ins). No page says 'back-in' in words, so I did not write false; consider clearing it.

SITE COUNT: the map shows 20 pads: 16 daily, 3 'Permanent' (#5, #19, #20, likely seasonal) and a host pad (#4). Only #1 and #8-#15 are bookable online; how the other daily pads are let is not stated, so fcfs is left unset.
Rig fit: site 1 'Best for camping units under 30 feet'; sites 8-15 are ~50 x 16 ft. A 23-ft rig fits. Note's 'May-September' was dropped in favor of the season group. Pin OK (centre of the loop).
